p256Note: Anvil 1.5 on Cancun does not serve the P-256 precompile at 0x100. The scenarios used secp256k1 keys. P-256 was not tested live.
phoneScreens: The phone screens were not clicked through.

scenarios.name: first-use
scenarios.detail: Activation in initCode deployed the account and rotated.

scenarios.name: spend after first use
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: send-and-rotate
scenarios.detail: One included send rotated once and paid.

scenarios.name: spend after a normal send
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: speed-up
scenarios.detail: The replacement at the same nonce landed, and the key rotated once.

scenarios.name: spend after a speed-up
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: cancel
scenarios.detail: The empty replacement landed. The payment did not.

scenarios.name: spend after a cancel
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: original-lands-first
scenarios.detail: The replacement was refused. The phone caught up to the included send.

scenarios.name: spend after a refused replacement
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: reverting-send
scenarios.detail: The key rotated and the receipt reported failure.

scenarios.name: spend after a reverting send
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: two-ops-one-bundle
scenarios.detail: Both operations executed in one bundle, each under its own validation.

scenarios.name: spend after two operations in one bundle
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: repeated-next-key-one-bundle
scenarios.detail: A to B, B to C, and C to B all executed in one bundle.

scenarios.name: spend after a repeated next key
scenarios.detail: A later send paid with the key that was just installed.

scenarios.name: old-device-first-use
scenarios.detail: A creation-time activation still deployed after about two years, and a later send paid.

scenarios.name: restored-device-first-use
scenarios.detail: Entering the words again rebuilt the same activation, and that activation deployed.

scenarios.name: new-network-first-use
scenarios.detail: A chain left out of creation needed the words, and those words signed its activation.

scenarios.name: stolen-phone-loses-race
scenarios.detail: Recovery opened the funded chain with a new key. The old activation was refused and the funds stayed.

scenarios.name: secure-all-outside-payer
scenarios.detail: An empty account and a token-only account both needed an outside payer. Paying closed the token account. The unpaid account still accepted the old activation.
